# Feature: Mule bot — sanity check

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Sanity-check candidate mechanic #40 (Mule bot) from Enemies and Bots before it is used in real levels. Effect: A follower that carries 4 extra inventory slots. Unique: a follower whose slots are inventory, not a switch holder. Useful: carry eight keys worth of gear in a four-slot game. Source status in the candidate file is 'revised'; it was revised from human review and is now treated as a trial candidate.

## User Story

**As a** player

**I want** a follower that carries 4 extra inventory slots.

**So that** carry eight keys worth of gear in a four-slot game.

## High-Level Use Case

The player meets Mule bot for the first time in its teaching room (mech-40-mule-bot-room). Teaching moment: First room: five keys and a twin lock in a four-slot game, with the mule bot behind a one-tile pinch. A player who fills their own slots first and backs into the pinch swaps places with the bot unexpectedly and has to restart the arrangement, which teaches that the bot's position and its four slots are part of the inventory. The sanity check plays that room, exercises every rule below, and records a replayable session.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Your base inventory is 4 slots
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: The bot follows the exact path you walked, one tile behind
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Keys it carries use its 4 slots, shown as a second HUD row
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: If you move backwards into it you swap tiles, so it never blocks you
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: It waits if its next path tile is a hazard and catches up along your path when it can

## Edge Cases & Rules

- If you move backwards into it you swap tiles, so it never blocks you
- Movement/state stays deterministic: state advances only through the pure step function with recorded t_ms; a recorded session replays to the same end state.
- Restart (R / restart) restores the room to its initial state, including this mechanic.

## UI / Feedback

- The player sees Mule bot's effect happen on its tile(s) exactly as the rules above describe; no hidden state.
- Any counter, inventory or HUD impact follows the rules above; if a rule needs a counter it is shown while it matters (see Open Questions).
- Failure in the teaching room returns the player to the room start / checkpoint for an immediate retry.

## Assets & Level Data Needed

- Level JSON: new Test Level mech-40-mule-bot-room (rows + legend) implementing the teaching moment above.
- Sprites/defs: reuse existing tiles where the mechanic reuses an existing tile; add a new sprite/tile def only if this mechanic introduces a new tile (confirm in the implement task).
- Source: plans/level-design/candidate-mechanics/enemies-and-bots.yml mechanic #40.

## Open Questions

- Human review to honour: Adding it would give us 4 more slots.
- Human review to honour: We have to consider it follows behind us.
- Human review to honour: So what happens if you move backwards? you swap spots so it never gets in your way.
- Synergies deferred to a later run (do not build now): Twin lock (11): the level that only fits if the mule carries the second key.
- Synergies deferred to a later run (do not build now): Swap tile (93): swap with your own bot to get its slots past a pinch.
